name: Golden-tufted Grackle
rangeDescription: Tepuis of southern venezuela to western guyana and northern brazil (roraima)
description: A medium-sized blackbird of tepui highland forests. Adults are entirely black except for yellow tufts at bend of wing; young birds are dull blackish-gray and lack the tufts.

name: Garnet-throated Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Mountains of southern mexico to guatemala, el salvador, and honduras
description: Large, spectacular, and solidly built hummingbird of humid evergreen and pine-evergreen forest in mountains; uncommon. Feeds at all levels on flowers and sometimes perches on prominent high twigs.

name: Black Crake
rangeDescription: Sub-saharan africa
description: A small, pudgy, blackish waterbird with reddish eyes, a yellowish bill, and diagnostic pink-red legs. The immature is browner, with duller legs and bill.

name: Greater Adjutant
rangeDescription: Formerly from northern india to vietnam, dispersing west to pakistan; currently breeds northeastern india (assam) and cambodia, with dispersal west to nepal
description: Immense and imposing undertaker of a stork with a bare head and neck, pale eyes, and dark gray wings. Overlaps in some areas with similar but smaller Lesser Adjutant; note pale wing panel, paler heavier bill, prominent white neck ruff, and when in flight, grayer and less contrasting underwing.

name: Paddyfield Warbler
rangeDescription: Central eurasia; winters in southern asia
description: Warm brown above and pale below; strong dark eyestripe contrasts with white eyebrow. Smallish reed warbler with long and strongly rounded tail, short bill with dark tip, and short primary projection.

name: Sulawesi Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern sulawesi
description: A dull warbler restricted to Sulawesi with a pale eyebrow, a largely blackish bill, dark legs, dingy olive-brown upperparts, and a pale yellow underside. No distinct wingbar.

name: Scaled Chachalaca
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil
description: Medium-sized chachalaca with brown plumage and a heavily scaled throat and upper breast. Found at forest edges and in second growth, where it forages in small groups on the ground and trees.

name: Spectacled Eider
rangeDescription: Breeds north-central and northeastern siberia from lena delta to chukotka, and western and northern alaska in yukon delta and arctic coastal plain; winters polynyas (ice-free seas) between st. lawrence and st. matthew islands (northern bering sea)
description: This peculiar Arctic sea duck breeds on the tundra in Alaska and far eastern Russia and winters in massive flocks among pack ice in the Bering Sea. Males have a unique olive-green head with white goggles, a dark breast, and a carrot-orange bill.

name: Akiapolaau
rangeDescription: Montane koa forest of hawaii
description: A rare Hawaiian honeycreeper of native forests above 5,000 feet elevation on Hawaii Island. Appears bigger-headed and shorter-tailed than other honeycreepers.

name: Sichuan Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Mountains of southern china
description: Like most leaf warblers, it is a small, active bird and excruciatingly difficult to identify; likely to be seen fleetingly in the upper layers of the forest. Very similar in appearance to other “Pallas’s-type” leaf warblers in its range.

name: White-backed Black-Tit
rangeDescription: Wooded mountain gorges of ethiopia and adjacent eritrea
description: An unusual tit that is mostly black with a pale back. Males have a bright white back and females and immatures a buff-colored one.

name: Bornean Forktail
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern borneo
description: A typical forktail, with piebald plumage and long tail. Black head, upper back, chest and wings; white belly, rump, forecrown and wingbar; black and white tail and pale-pink legs.

name: Asian Openbill
rangeDescription: Lowlands of indian subcontinent to southeastern asia
description: A relatively small stork species with a grayish to white body and black wings and tail with a hint of gloss. The Asian Openbill gets its name from a distinctive gap in the dull grayish yellow bill.

name: Plate-billed Mountain-Toucan
rangeDescription: Andes of southwestern colombia to southern ecuador
description: Extraordinary and iconic toucan of Andean cloud forest in northwestern Ecuador, just barely reaching southwestern Colombia. Plumage is colorful, with blue underparts, coppery back, black crown and nape, red undertail coverts, and yellow crescent below eye.

name: Brown Rock Chat
rangeDescription: Rocky hills and cliffs of northeastern pakistan and northern india
description: Plain chocolate-brown chat, often seen standing tall and proud on ridges, cliff edges, and buildings. Female Indian Robin can be somewhat similar; note Brown Rock Chat’s proportionally shorter tail and lack of a rufous vent.

name: Black-breasted Wood-Quail
rangeDescription: Tropical and subtropical forest of costa rica and western panama
description: Plump chickenlike bird, stout bill, dark brown overall with blacker breast and face and variable white markings on throat. The blackness of the breast should help separate from other quail.

name: Flat-billed Vireo
rangeDescription: Semiarid lowland scrub of hispaniola including gonâve island
description: A small, slow-moving species that prefers dry brush and scrublands where it typically feeds low and sometimes even on the ground; sometimes found at higher elevations where it can be found feeding in or near the canopy in vine tangles. The Flat-billed Vireo is a relatively plain species, with bold white wingbars, and whitish eyes.

name: New Zealand King Shag
rangeDescription: Islands in cook strait (new zealand)
description: A large, thick-necked black-and-white marine shag endemic to the Marlborough Sounds of New Zealand. Shows pink feet, a distinct white patch on the wings, and a blue eye-ring.

name: White-headed Vulture
rangeDescription: Thornscrub and desert of sub-saharan africa
description: A medium-sized, mostly dark vulture with an angular, naked, pale pink head and bulky coral-colored beak. In flight, the adult’s white “armpits” extend out as a stripe along the middle of the underwing; the larger females differ from males by having all-white innermost flight feathers.

name: Patagonian Mockingbird
rangeDescription: Central and southern argentina and southern chile
description: Fairly common in Argentine Patagonia, but local and scarce in southern Chile. Favors semiopen habitats, from shrub-steppe to farmland with hedges and shrubby patches.
